questions.question_prompt: The speed limit is 70 km/h and a bus signals to leave its stop. Which statement is correct?
questions.keyed_answer: The bus must give way, but you should still be ready to cooperate.
questions.teaching_excerpt: The threshold concerns the maximum permitted speed on the road, not how fast you happen to be travelling. At a 70 km/h limit, the special bus-stop departure rule above does not apply. The bus must wait for an entry that can be made without danger or unnecessary obstruction. You still have a duty to adapt speed to facilitate an observed entry into your lane. A bus indicator does not create unconditional priority, and the higher road limit does not excuse deliberately blocking it. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§43–45 Road limit Duties when the bus signals to leave its stop 50 km/h or lower Slow and let the bus leave; stop if needed. The bus driver must take particular care. 70 km/h, ordinary entry into your lane The special bus-exit duty does not apply. The bus waits for a safe entry; you adapt speed to facilitate the observed entry. Safety advice · Let a guide dog work. Do not pet, call
questions.coverage_reasoning: All three essential claims taught: ≤50 special opportunity/stop duty, safe bus entry at 70, and continued cooperation under §43. Explicitly distinguishes road limit from actual speed; original 40 km/h bus example extended to a 70 km/h comparison.

questions.question_prompt: How should you behave around a guide dog working in traffic?
questions.teaching_excerpt: Do not pet, call to or talk to a working guide dog to attract its attention. Distraction can endanger the person it is helping. Allow the pair room and time; if you need to communicate, address the handler rather than trying to direct the dog. The handler chooses the route and remains in control. For example, a passenger beside your parked car wants to greet a guide dog at a crossing. Ask them to leave it working and keep the path clear. MFD: meeting a working guide dog Traffic terminology · A bicycle is a vehicle. A person riding an ordinary pedal bicycle is operating a vehicle, even without an engine. “Vehicle” does not mean only “motor vehicle”. Apply the relevant cyclist duties and protections; crossing distinctions remain in M04-L03. Transportstyrelsen: bicycle definition
questions.coverage_reasoning: Avoids attention directed at the working dog; explains handler risk, communication with handler and a guide-dog interaction example.
